```{r,include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse) #always
library(ape) #for evo analysis

```

# Introduction

The highly-diverse genus *Anolis* contains over 400 species, making it the most speciose genus within the Amniota. In this study, we seek to examine the relationship between snout-vent length (SVL) and total hind-limb length (HTotal). Previously, the hind limb-ecomorph relationship has been studied in anoles [@hagey2017there]. We will perform a residual analysis to determine how this relationship varies with ecomorph, and we will utilize Brownian Motion and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model fitting to correct for phylogenetic non-independence. 

<center>
![An *Anolis* lizard](https://encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcRH7oW9KFBNAzQXxdtuwt3osbP58QFBkML8xNVduK6k1wkyEQJe5se9iAcj&s=10)
</center>

# Methods

Morphological and ecomorphological data from 46 species of anole were combined and filtered by species to produce data on mean snout-vent length (`SVL`, length between the snout and the vent, i.e., anus, a standard for reptiles), and the mean total hind-limb length (`HTotal`). A linear model first was created to plot `SVL` versus `HTotal`, followed by a non-linear allometric one. The fit of these models was compared using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). 

Next, using data from an anole phylogenetic tree [@poe2017phylogenetic] the effect of ecomorphology on the hindlimb-SVL relationships was taken into account

# Results

We uncovered a significant effect from the parameters ArbPD and the combination of ArbPD and PH. The most optimal model under AIC was the combination model, which differed from the ArbPD model by ~1.7. Residual modeling displays disparate effects for grass-bush and trunk-ground ecomorphs compared to others.


```{r, "load the data"}
anole <- read_csv("anole.dat.csv")
anole.eco <- read_csv("anole.eco.csv")
anole.tree <- read.tree("anole.tre")
```
```{r, "join, filter, mutate to log"}
anole2 <- anole %>%
  left_join(anole.eco) %>%
  filter(!Ecomorph %in% c("U", "CH")) %>%
  na.omit()

anole.log <- anole2 %>%
  mutate_at(c("SVL", "HTotal", "PH", "ArbPD"),log)
```
```{r, "PGLS models"}
### phylogenetic GLS models

#PGLS under BM, no ecomorph
pgls.BM1 <- gls(HTotal ~SVL, correlation = corBrownian(1,phy = anole.tree,form=~Species),data = anole.log, method = "ML")

#PGLS under BM, w ecomorph
pgls.BM2 <- gls(HTotal ~SVL * Ecomorph2, correlation = corBrownian(1,phy = anole.tree,form=~Species),data = anole.log, method = "ML")

#PGLS under OU, no ecomorph
pgls.OU1 <-  gls(HTotal ~SVL, correlation = corMartins(0,phy = anole.tree,form=~Species),data = anole.log, method = "ML")

#PGLS under OU, w ecomorph
pgls.OU2 <-  gls(HTotal ~SVL * Ecomorph2, correlation = corMartins(0,phy = anole.tree,form=~Species),data = anole.log, method = "ML")
```
```{r, "AIC"}
#AIC operations
anole.phylo.aic <- AICc(pgls.BM1,pgls.BM2,pgls.OU1,pgls.OU2)
anole.phylow.aicw <- aicw(anole.phylo.aic$AICc)
```
```{r, "AIC-table"}
anole.phylo.aic["AICc"] %>%
  kable(
    rownames = "Model",
    caption = "AIC values for the four PGLS models under Brownian motion and Ornstein–Uhlenbeck evolution, with and without ecomorph.")
```
```{r, "add residuals"}
#add phylo-corrected residuals 
anole.log <- anole.log %>%
  mutate(phylo.res=residuals(pgls.BM2))
```
```{r "regression-plot", fig.cap="Log-transformed total hindlimb length (HTotal) versus log-transformed snout-vent length (SVL), with points and regression lines colored by anole ecomorph. Lines show ordinary linear regressions within each ecomorph."}
#plot regression
anole.log %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = SVL, y = HTotal, color = Ecomorph2)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "ln(Snout-vent length)",
    y = "ln(Total hindlimb length)",
    color = "Ecomorph"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r, "plot residuals", fig.cap="Boxplot of phylogenetically corrected hindlimb residuals versus anole ecomorph"}
#plot residuals 
p.eco.phylo <- anole.log %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Ecomorph2,y=phylo.res)) +geom_boxplot() +stat_summary(fun=mean, geom="point", size=3)

print(p.eco.phylo)
```

# Discussion

Brownian Motion modeling and AIC testing suggest that the SVL~HTotal relationship is significantly affected by ArbPD and the combination between ArbPD and PH. PH alone is insufficient to account for the data. Residual analysis shows that the SVL~HTotal relationship experiences different effects for the grass-bush and trunk-ground ecomorphs compared to the crown-giant, trunk, trunk-crown, and twig ecomorphs.
